PREFACE前言
IN 1977, Scholars Press (Atlanta, Georgia) published the first edition of Orphic Hymns: Text, Translation and Notes by Apostolos N. Athanassakis for the Society of Biblical Literature’s Texts and Translations, Graeco-Roman Religion Series. The text used for that edition, as for the present one, is that by Wilhelm Quandt. Occasionally Gabriella Ricciardelli’s more recent text was also consulted for the present edition. The translation from the first edition has been revisited and rejuvenated. In all cases which involve change the purpose has been to attain a greater flow, especially such as is appropriate to a sacred text consisting of lengthy lists of epithets. The introduction is more comprehensive and the notes offer the reader much more information. It is hoped that the indices will be a welcome addition.1977 年，学者出版社（位于佐治亚州亚特兰大）为圣经文学学会的文本与翻译系列、希腊罗马宗教分册出版了阿波斯托洛斯·N·阿萨纳萨基斯所著《俄耳甫斯颂歌：文本、翻译与注释》的第一版。该版本所使用的文本，与当前版本一样，均基于威廉·昆特的版本。在准备当前版本时，偶尔也参考了加布里埃拉·里恰尔代利较新的文本。第一版的翻译经过了重新审视和更新。在所有涉及修改的情况下，目的都是为了获得更流畅的译文，特别是对于由冗长称号列表组成的神圣文本而言，这种流畅性尤为合适。引言部分更为全面，注释为读者提供了更多信息。希望索引部分能成为受欢迎的补充。
Professor Athanassakis wishes to express his warmest thanks to Miss Allison Emily Page for her patient assistance in the preparation of substantial portions of the book. INTRODUCTION引言
ANTIQITY is virtually silent on the Orphic Hymns. The oldest reference to them is found in a scholium on Hesiod’s Theogony by Ioannes Galenos (first half of the twelfth century AD). Galenos refers to them three times in the same scholium but says nothing about their authorship or literary value.关于俄耳甫斯颂歌，古代文献几乎保持沉默。现存最古老的记载见于约翰内斯·加莱诺斯（公元 12 世纪上半叶）对赫西俄德《神谱》的注疏中。加莱诺斯在同一处注疏中三次提及这些颂歌，但未言及其作者或文学价值。
The first manuscript of the Hymns to reach the West was the one carried to Venice by Giovanni Aurispa in 1423. It seems that another manuscript was taken to Italy by Franciscus Philadelphus four years later in 1427. Both of these manuscripts, and perhaps four others, have been lost. The loss of the manuscript brought to Venice by Aurispa is especially regrettable since it may have served as the archetype of all surviving codices. Of these we have thirty-six, twenty-five on paper and eleven on skin. Some of these codices contain only a portion of the Hymns. The same codices frequently contain the Homeric hymns, Hesiodea, the Orphic Argonautika, and the hymns of Proclus and Kallimakhos. As for the date of these codices, it seems safe to infer that they were all copied between 1450 and 1550.最早传入西方的颂歌手稿是乔瓦尼·奥里斯帕于 1423 年带到威尼斯的那份。似乎还有另一份手稿在四年后的 1427 年由弗朗西斯科·费拉德菲斯带往意大利。这两份手稿，或许还有其他四份，均已散佚。奥里斯帕携至威尼斯的手稿失传尤为可惜，因为它可能是现存所有抄本的祖本。现存抄本共三十六份，其中二十五份为纸质，十一份为羊皮纸。部分抄本仅收录颂歌的片段。这些抄本中常同时收录荷马颂歌、赫西俄德作品、俄耳甫斯《阿尔戈英雄纪》以及普罗克洛斯与卡利马科斯的颂诗。关于抄本年代，现有证据表明它们均抄写于 1450 年至 1550 年间。
We have reason to believe that the codex Aurispa brought with him from Constantinople in 1423 stirred up considerable excitement among the learned. On the other hand, it may not have been until the arrival in Venice of the Greek sage Georgios Gemistos (usually surnamed Plethon) sometime in the middle of the fifteenth century that the Italians really took notice of the Orphic Hymns. The editio princeps was printed in Florence in 1500. It also contains the Orphic Argonautica and some of the hymns of Proclus. By the year 1600 there were five more editions, one of which was Aldine’s, published in 1517. From the editions that followed in subsequent centuries the one that excels all others—perhaps to this day—is Gottfried Hermann’s 1805 work. Abel’s edition in 1885 has been received with adverse criticism. Wilhelm Quandt had finished his edition by 1941, but the vicissitudes of the war forced most scholars to wait until 1955 to reap the benefits of his labors from its reprinted and somewhat augmented version.我们有理由相信，奥里斯帕于 1423 年从君士坦丁堡带回的手抄本在学术界引起了相当大的轰动。另一方面，可能直到十五世纪中叶希腊智者乔治奥斯·杰米斯托斯（通常姓氏为普莱松）抵达威尼斯时，意大利人才真正开始关注《俄耳甫斯颂歌》。首版印刷于 1500 年在佛罗伦萨问世，其中还包含了《俄耳甫斯阿尔戈英雄纪》以及普罗克洛斯的若干颂歌。到 1600 年为止，又出现了五个版本，其中之一是阿尔定出版社于 1517 年出版的。在随后几个世纪出版的版本中，戈特弗里德·赫尔曼于 1805 年的作品超越了所有其他版本——或许至今仍是如此。阿贝尔于 1885 年的版本受到了负面批评。威廉·昆特在 1941 年完成了他的版本，但战争的动荡迫使大多数学者等到 1955 年，才从其重印并略有增补的版本中收获他辛勤劳动的成果。
A date of composition cannot be assigned to the Hymns with any certainty. A few ancient sources make direct or oblique references to Orphic hymns, but they need not refer to our Hymns. It is much more reasonable to assume that the expression “Hymns of Orpheus” (e.g., Plato Laws 829d–e, Pausanias 9.30.12) does not refer to a specific collection such as the one at our disposal but rather to Orphic poetry—perhaps even of the oral variety—that was attributed to the founder of Orphism. In the first oration against Aristogeiton, Pseudo-Demosthenes tells us that “Orpheus says that she [Dike] sits beside the throne of Zeus and watches over all human matters” (25.11). The similarity between this statement and lines 2–3 in the hymn to Dike (hymn 62) has been noticed, but it would be unwise to build a hypothesis of composition on what must have become a common metaphor.1无法确定《颂歌》的具体创作年代。一些古代文献直接或间接提及俄耳甫斯颂歌，但这些未必指代我们手中的《颂歌》。更合理的推测是，"俄耳甫斯颂歌"（如柏拉图《法律篇》829d–e、保萨尼阿斯 9.30.12）并非特指我们现有的这种具体诗集，而是泛指归名于俄耳甫斯教派创始人的俄耳甫斯诗歌——甚至可能包含口传形式。在《反阿里斯托吉顿第一篇演说》中，伪狄摩西尼提到："俄耳甫斯说，她[狄刻]端坐于宙斯王座之侧，监察人间万事"（25.11）。虽然此论述与《狄刻颂》（第 62 首）第 2–3 行存在相似性，但基于这种可能已成为普遍隐喻的表述来构建创作假说并不明智。 1 
But the Orphic Hymns still may have existed quite early and gone unnoticed. After all, antiquity treated the much older Homeric hymns with astonishing indifference. Those scholars who place the composition of the Orphic Hymns within the first four centuries of our era are probably closer to the truth. The relative purity of the language and the nearly flawless hexameter would argue for the earlier part of this period. So would also the remarkable absence of anything faintly Christian. There is a syncretism, but the syncretism is that of unmistakably pagan elements. The content of the Hymns themselves yields nothing certain. However, the hymn to Apollon (hymn 34) contains some specific musical technical terms, and the collocation of ideas in lines 16–23 strongly suggests that the composer was at least vaguely familiar with Ptolemy’s Harmonics.2 This would provide a terminus post quem of about 200 AD. It is true that we have scant evidence for the existence of Orphic cults in the later Roman imperial period. On the other hand, the predilection of the Severan dynasty (193 to 235 AD) for Eastern institutions and ideas favored a movement for religious reform and a tolerance that eventually culminated in the resuscitation and flourishing of many mystic, especially Dionysian, cults. It may have been exactly in this sort of climate and at such a time that underground remnants of Orphism surfaced again to reassert the tenacity of the legendary divine musician of Thrace. Perhaps then a date in the middle of the third century AD is as good a guess as any.然而，俄耳甫斯颂歌可能早已存在，只是未被察觉。毕竟，古代对更为古老的荷马颂歌也表现出惊人的漠视。那些将俄耳甫斯颂歌的创作时间定于公元最初四个世纪的学者，或许更接近真相。语言的相对纯净和近乎完美的六步格律，都支持这一时期的早期阶段。同样，其中完全没有丝毫基督教色彩也令人瞩目。存在融合现象，但融合的是明确无误的异教元素。颂歌本身的内容并未提供确凿证据。不过，献给阿波罗的颂歌（第 34 首）包含一些具体的音乐术语，第 16 至 23 行中的思想排列强烈暗示，创作者至少对托勒密的《和声学》有所了解。 2 这将提供一个大约公元 200 年的创作时间下限。确实，关于罗马帝国后期俄耳甫斯崇拜存在的证据寥寥无几。 另一方面，塞维鲁王朝（公元 193 年至 235 年）对东方制度和思想的偏好，促进了宗教改革运动与宽容氛围，最终导致许多神秘主义教派——尤其是狄俄尼索斯崇拜——得以复兴并蓬勃发展。或许正是在这样的时代背景下，俄耳甫斯教的地下残余势力重新浮出水面，再次彰显了这位色雷斯传奇神乐师的顽强生命力。因此，将时间推测在公元三世纪中叶，或许是最合理的推断。
The place in which the Hymns were composed and originally used is a mystery. The appearance in the Hymns of divinities hardly known or totally unknown to mainland Greece should turn our attention eastward to Asia Minor, where, in fact, the names of some of these less known Asiatic gods have been consistently turning up in inscriptions. The three most telling names are Mise, Hipta, and Melinoe, all three previously known only from the Hymns until the soil of western Anatolia revealed their existence in inscriptions. Otto Kern in 1911 was the first to suggest that Pergamum was the birthplace of the Hymns and that they were used in mystic Dionysian ceremonies in the temenos of Demeter in the city. His suggestion has found both sympathizers and critics among scholars. Until epigraphic and other evidence points to some other place we might consider Kern’s theory a distinct possibility.《俄耳甫斯颂歌》的创作地点及其最初的使用场合至今仍是一个谜。颂歌中出现的某些神祇在希腊大陆几乎不为人知或完全陌生，这应当将我们的注意力引向东方的小亚细亚。事实上，这些较为鲜为人知的亚洲神祇的名字，在铭文中屡见不鲜。最具说服力的三个名字是米塞、希普塔和梅利诺厄，在安纳托利亚西部的土壤通过铭文揭示它们的存在之前，这三个名字此前仅见于《俄耳甫斯颂歌》。奥托·克恩于 1911 年首次提出，帕加马是这些颂歌的诞生地，并且它们被用于该城得墨忒耳圣域中神秘的狄俄尼索斯仪式。他的这一观点在学者中既有支持者，也有批评者。在铭文或其他证据指向其他地点之前，我们或许可以将克恩的理论视为一种明显的可能性。

The Orphic Hymns constitute a distinct collection, and they should be seen as one part of a vast ancient literature that modern scholars label “Orphic.” However, the term “Orphic” is somewhat misleading. It implies something unified, stable, and definable—something like a movement, a genre, a type of phenomenon. But in actuality “Orphic” is a sort of catch-all term that is used to designate anything and everything directly or indirectly connected to Orpheus. And who this figure was leads to even more ambiguity. We do not know if he ever existed. Traditionally he was from the wilds of Thrace, a foreigner to the Greeks, and a bard of great renown, sometimes thought to be even earlier than Homer and Hesiod. He was so proficient with his stringed instrument, the lyre, that he could sway inanimate objects and even bring the lord and lady of the dead to tears. In addition to his amazing musical talents, he knew of secret rites, usually those of Dionysos, and particularly those dealing with the salvation of the soul after death, and these he taught to his fellow man in the form of mysteries. Indeed, Orpheus himself descended to the land of death in order to win back his beloved Eurydike, who had died before her time. His tragic failure has become one of the most haunting legacies bequeathed to us by the poets of old. There were in fact a number of poems in circulation attributed to Orpheus in the ancient world. Some seem to have been quite old, perhaps even pre-Classical, but others were composed at a later time and claimed to be his. These poems have come down to us in fragments, quoted or alluded to in an astonishing variety of authors from all periods, in both prose and poetry and in both Greek and Latin. The fragments are assiduously collected in Bernabé’s Teubner edition. While geared to scholars, even readers with little or no knowledge of ancient languages will find it a useful resource. Bernabé gathers the primary sources, and, with a little tenacity in learning the abbreviations for author and work, one can easily track down a suitable English translation for most of them.《俄耳甫斯颂歌》构成了一部独特的合集，它们应被视为现代学者所称"俄耳甫斯式"浩瀚古代文献的一部分。然而，"俄耳甫斯式"这个术语具有一定误导性。它暗示着某种统一、稳定且可定义的事物——类似一场运动、一种文体或一类现象。但实际上，"俄耳甫斯式"是个包罗万象的术语，用以指代任何与俄耳甫斯直接或间接相关的事物。而关于这位人物本身则存在更多模糊性。我们无从考证他是否真实存在过。传统上他被认为来自色雷斯的蛮荒之地，对希腊人而言是个异乡人，同时也是位声名显赫的吟游诗人，有时甚至被认为早于荷马与赫西俄德。他手持弦乐器里拉琴的技艺如此精湛，竟能打动无生命之物，甚至令冥府之主与其伴侣潸然泪下。除了惊人的音乐天赋，他还通晓秘仪——通常是关于狄俄尼索斯的仪式，特别是涉及死后灵魂救赎的秘仪，并以奥秘教义的形式将这些知识传授给人类同胞。 确实，俄耳甫斯本人曾下到冥界，试图带回他早逝的爱人欧律狄刻。他悲剧性的失败已成为古代诗人留给我们最令人难忘的遗产之一。事实上，在古代世界流传着许多被归为俄耳甫斯所作的诗篇。其中一些似乎相当古老，甚至可能早于古典时期，但另一些则是后世创作并声称出自他手。这些诗篇以片段形式流传至今，被各个时期众多作者以散文或诗歌、希腊语或拉丁语的形式引用或提及，其多样性令人惊叹。这些片段被精心收录在贝尔纳韦的托伊布纳版本中。虽然该书面向学者，但即使对古代语言知之甚少或一无所知的读者也会发现它是一个有用的资源。 贝尔纳韦收集了主要来源，只要稍加坚持学习作者和作品的缩写，人们就能轻松为其中大部分内容找到合适的英文翻译。
Two notable Orphic documents may be mentioned here. The first one is an extremely important papyrus text that was discovered in Macedonia in 1962, known as the Derveni Papyrus and datable to the second half of the fourth century BC. It is in a lacunose state, but there is ample enough material to determine that the author was writing a philosophical interpretation of some theogonic poem he ascribes to Orpheus.3 Another is a group known as the Bacchic gold tablets. There are thirty-nine of these, dating from 400 BC to 200 AD, found from Rome to Asia Minor, from Macedonia to Krete. They are inscriptions on thin gold leaf that were found in graves. Some just have a name, presumably of the person buried, who was an initiate in the mysteries. Some contain instructions for the soul on what to do once it arrives at the underworld in order to secure its special dispensation, its reward for being initiated in the mysteries while living.4这里可以提及两份重要的俄耳甫斯文献。第一份是 1962 年在马其顿发现的极为重要的纸莎草文本，被称为德尔维尼纸莎草，可追溯至公元前四世纪下半叶。该文献虽残缺不全，但现有材料足以表明作者正在对一首他归功于俄耳甫斯的神谱诗进行哲学阐释。 3 另一份文献是一组被称为酒神金箔的文物。共有三十九片，年代从公元前 400 年至公元 200 年，发现地点从罗马到小亚细亚，从马其顿到克里特岛。这些是刻在薄金片上的铭文，出土于墓葬中。有些仅刻有名字，推测为墓主——即秘仪入会者——的姓名。另一些则包含对灵魂的指引，教导其抵达冥界后应如何行事，以确保获得特殊恩典，即生前入会所得的奖赏。 4 
One important fact that clearly emerges from this “Orphic” literature is that there had developed what we may call an “Orphic” mythology, one that appropriated much from the “official” mythologies in Homer and Hesiod but extended them in idiosyncratic ways. Cosmogony/theogony was a widely disseminated type, although there were numerous variations. Three versions were preserved by the Neoplatonist Damascius, who attributed one to the Peripatetic Eudemos and another to a certain Hieronymos and/or Hellanikos and who cited a third from a poem he called the Orphic Rhapsodies (probably the same as the one that appears elsewhere under the title of Sacred Discourses in Twenty-Four Rhapsodies).5 Despite these many and convoluted accounts, certain details are found again and again in our sources with enough consistency that we can at times with some confidence designate something as “Orphic” or at least influenced by “Orphic” literature. Our collection is “Orphic” in this sense.从这份“俄耳甫斯”文献中清晰浮现的一个重要事实是，已经发展出了一种我们可称之为“俄耳甫斯”神话的体系。这种神话大量借鉴了荷马与赫西俄德作品中的“官方”神话，却又以独特的方式对其进行了延伸拓展。宇宙起源论/神谱学是一种广泛传播的类型，尽管存在诸多变体。新柏拉图主义者达马斯基乌斯保存了三个版本：其一被他归于漫步学派的欧德摩斯，另一版归于某位希罗尼穆斯和/或赫拉尼库斯，他还从一首他称为《俄耳甫斯狂想诗》的作品中引用了第三个版本（很可能与别处以《二十四狂想诗中的神圣论述》为题出现的版本相同）。 5 尽管存在这些纷繁复杂的叙述，某些细节在我们的资料来源中反复出现，具有足够的一致性，使我们有时能较有把握地将某些内容认定为“俄耳甫斯式”的，或至少是受到“俄耳甫斯”文献影响的。我们的这部诗集正是在这个意义上属于“俄耳甫斯”传统。

There is little to force us to the assumption of a single authorship for all the Hymns. Indeed, we can scarcely assume that the collection was composed at once. The opening to Mousaios, for example, has come under suspicion.6 However, the Hymns do give the impression of being the work of a religious antiquary who had ready access to some sort of concordance from which he marshaled forth hosts of epithets that he then linked together in hexameters. This is more or less the view of Christian Lobeck, a view that is bound to be shared by those who consider the Hymns literary rather than religious documents. Albrecht Dieterich and Kern, and later William Guthrie, have taken exception to this opinion. It is reasonable to think that when in the third century AD many Dionysian cults were revived and made to serve as a convenient umbrella for the resurrection of Orphic elements, revered literary sources and earlier ritual practices, such as the Eleusinian mysteries, were tapped for the creation of appropriate cult literature. Every religion known to man is an amalgamation of various religious movements. Here we must mention the concept of the bricoleur suggested by Fritz Graf and Sarah Johnston in discussing how the peculiar Orphic mythology might have been developed.7几乎没有证据迫使我们假设所有《俄耳甫斯颂歌》均出自单一作者之手。事实上，我们很难认为这部合集是一次性创作完成的。例如，献给穆赛俄斯的开篇部分就曾受到质疑。 6 然而，这些颂歌确实给人一种印象：它们是一位宗教古籍研究者的作品，他手头备有某种索引汇编，从中调集了大量修饰语，然后将它们以六步格诗的形式串联起来。这大致是克里斯蒂安·洛贝克的观点，那些视这些颂歌为文学作品而非宗教文献的人，也必然会认同这一看法。阿尔布雷希特·迪特里希和克恩，以及后来的威廉·格思里，对此观点持有异议。有理由认为，在公元三世纪，许多狄俄尼索斯教派复兴，并成为复活俄耳甫斯元素、尊崇文学来源和早期仪式实践（如厄琉息斯秘仪）的便利庇护所时，人们便借鉴这些资源来创作合适的教派文献。人类已知的每一种宗教都是各种宗教运动的融合体。 在此必须提及弗里茨·格拉夫与莎拉·约翰斯顿提出的"拼装者"概念，用以解释这种独特的俄耳甫斯神话体系可能如何形成。 7 
The Hymns stand as a particular example of a very old genre that survived throughout antiquity. A hymn is essentially a poem sung in praise of a god, often with a request or prayer. The word “hymn” can be used as a generic term, or to designate a specific genre, such as Pindar’s hymns. Over time, a wide variety developed. A hymn might contain narrative, long or short, such as some of the Homeric hymns. A hymn might have cultic function, such as the Kretan hymn found at Palaikastro that invokes Zeus as the greatest kouros (fourth century BC, possibly older). A hymn can be purely lyrical, such as those of Mesomedes (mid-second century AD), some of whose works survive with musical notation. We find hymns as dedications, inscribed on pillars or walls, such as the four hymns by Isidoros of the Fayum (88–80 BC). Some scraps of poetry found in the magical papyri, often metrically faulty, have been titled “hymns” by scholars, but one should regard the reconstructed versions by the editor of the papyri, Karl Preisendanz, with caution. Philosophers wrote hymns, too, such as the Stoic Kleanthes’ Hymn to Zeus (early- to mid-third century BC) and the surviving group by the Neoplatonist Proclus (fifth century AD). Prose was also a vehicle for hymns. The story of Atlantis that Kritias tells is prefaced with a thanks to Sokrates and also noted as a kind of hymn in honor of Athene, whose festival, the Panathenaia, was taking place (Plato Timaios 21a). A number of prose hymns were written by Aelius Aristides (mid-second century AD). Hymns can also be embedded in other works. In Apuleius’ Metamorphoses, Lucius has had it with being a literal ass, and, after bathing himself seven times in a river (seven being a holy number according to Pythagoras), he invokes Isis the moon goddess in hymnic style (11.2). Finally, Ovid, as one would expect, plays with the genre when he has his lovesick Apollon call out to the fleeing Daphne the identity of her pursuer in terms that are typical of the genre: a list of favorite cult sites and the wide powers of the divinity addressed (Metamorphoses 1.515–524). The joke is that it is the god himself, not the petitioner, who utters the hymn; the inversion is both a mocking and serious testament to the power of love.8这些颂歌是古代流传下来的一个非常古老文体的特殊范例。颂歌本质上是一首赞美神的诗歌，通常包含请求或祈祷。"颂歌"一词可作为通用术语，也可指特定文体，如品达的颂歌。随着时间的推移，颂歌发展出多种形式。有些颂歌包含长短不一的叙事，例如荷马颂歌中的某些作品。有些颂歌具有祭祀功能，如在帕莱卡斯特罗发现的克里特颂歌，将宙斯称为最伟大的青年神（公元前四世纪，可能更早）。有些颂歌纯粹是抒情性的，例如梅索梅德斯的作品（公元二世纪中期），他的部分作品还保留着乐谱。我们还发现作为献词的颂歌，刻在柱子或墙壁上，例如法尤姆的伊西多罗斯的四首颂歌（公元前 88-80 年）。在魔法纸莎草中发现的一些诗歌片段，虽然韵律常有瑕疵，但被学者们冠以"颂歌"之名，不过对于纸莎草编辑卡尔·普赖森丹茨重构的版本，我们应持谨慎态度。 哲学家们也创作赞美诗，例如斯多葛学派克莱安西斯（公元前三世纪早中期）的《宙斯颂》，以及新柏拉图主义者普罗克洛斯（公元五世纪）留存下来的作品集。散文同样成为赞美诗的载体。克里提亚斯讲述的亚特兰蒂斯故事，开篇便向苏格拉底致谢，并注明这是为雅典娜女神献上的一种颂歌——当时正值她的庆典帕那忒那亚节举行之际（柏拉图《蒂迈欧篇》21a）。埃利乌斯·阿里斯提德斯（公元二世纪中期）创作了多篇散文体赞美诗。赞美诗亦可嵌入其他作品之中。在阿普列乌斯的《变形记》中，卢修斯受够了做一头真正的驴，在河中沐浴七次（根据毕达哥拉斯学说，七乃神圣之数）后，他以颂歌风格向月神伊西斯祈祷（11.2）。最后，正如人们所料，奥维德对这一体裁进行了戏仿：他让陷入情网的阿波罗对逃亡的达芙妮喊出追逐者的身份，其措辞正是此类体裁的典型特征——列举受崇拜的圣地清单，并详述所祈愿神祇的广大权能（《变形记》1.515–524）。 笑话在于，吟唱颂歌的并非祈求者，而是神明本身；这种颠倒既是对爱情力量的戏谑，也是庄重的见证。 8 
Our composer has freely drawn on this venerable tradition. In addition to literature and religion, philosophy, too, has made its mark, though it is difficult to adduce parallels with certainty. Stoicism seems to have been particularly influential. Such hymns as those to Ether, the Stars, Physis, Boreas, Zephyros, Notos, being personifications of natural phenomena, may point to Stoic influence. So may the invocation of Pronoia (Providence) in the proemic piece (line 30). The prominence of the fiery element as found, e.g., in hymns 5.4 and 66.4–5 would further appear to reflect Stoic belief. Yet it could be argued for some of these (and others) that the deciding influence was from the Pre-Socratics (e.g., Empedokles, Herakleitos), Pythagoreanism, and even Neoplatonism or Neopythagoreanism. There is so much fusion of different philosophical ideas in this collection that the only thing that can be said of them in this regard is that they represent a confluence and a monument to the syncretism that characterized religion in general during the Hellenistic and especially Imperial era. Their composer was not interested in creating a religious or philosophical system. The initiates wanted to protect their lives and save their souls. And to this end they needed the good will of every god and every daimōn. The texts that they used in their rites are interesting not so much as poetry but as repositories of religious ideas, frequently borrowed from a wide range of older literature and expressed by a means peculiar to a category of the hymnic genre. Careful linguistic study of the provenance of many of the epithets in the hymns—especially the hapax legomena—may help us answer some of the vexing questions that surround them.我们的作曲家自由地汲取了这一古老传统。除了文学与宗教，哲学也留下了印记，尽管难以确切地找到相似之处。斯多葛学派似乎影响尤为深远。那些献给以太、星辰、自然、北风、西风、南风等自然现象拟人化的颂歌，可能指向斯多葛主义的影响。序诗（第 30 行）中对普罗诺亚（天命）的呼唤亦是如此。火元素的重要性，例如在颂歌 5.4 和 66.4–5 中，似乎进一步反映了斯多葛信仰。然而，对于其中一些（及其他）颂歌，也可以认为决定性影响来自前苏格拉底哲学家（如恩培多克勒、赫拉克利特）、毕达哥拉斯主义，甚至新柏拉图主义或新毕达哥拉斯主义。这部作品中融合了如此多不同的哲学思想，以至于在这方面唯一能说的是，它们代表了希腊化时期，尤其是帝国时代宗教普遍特征的融合潮流与纪念碑。其作曲家无意创建一套宗教或哲学体系。 入会者渴望守护生命、拯救灵魂。为此，他们需要获得每一位神祇与精灵的眷顾。这些仪式中使用的文本，其价值不仅在于诗性，更在于它们是宗教思想的宝库——这些思想常借鉴自古籍经典，并通过颂歌这一独特体裁得以表达。对颂诗中诸多称号（尤其是那些仅出现一次的独特词汇）进行细致的语言溯源研究，或许能帮助我们解开围绕它们的诸多谜题。

Like all religions, Orphism had its profound religious beliefs and taboos. The animal sacrifice has a very special place in Greek religion. Those who participate are witnesses to the proper execution of the ritual that involves the sacrificial meal, always performed as an affirmation of shared religious beliefs. It is no accident that Orphism preached respect for animal life and abstention from eating the flesh of animals. Belief in the transmigration of souls, originally a Pythagorean one, made this prohibition necessary. For the Orphics, purification from guilt and pollution was a spiritual necessity, especially since they believed that punishment for wrongs committed in this world was inevitable. If it did not take place in a man’s lifetime, it would certainly happen in the subsequent one. The things from which an Orphic had to abstain threatened the purity of his soul with miasma, pollution. Purification, katharsis, did not simply free the soul from impurity but also protected a person from punishment and gave him the hope of eternal life in Elysium. Those who reached the underworld and its various punishments, all borrowed from Greek mythology, stayed there. They were then the unredeemed, doomed to be eternally deprived of the transmigration of their soul and thus the chance for redemption.9与所有宗教一样，俄耳甫斯教拥有其深刻的宗教信仰与禁忌。动物献祭在希腊宗教中占据着极其特殊的地位。参与者见证着仪式的正确执行，这包括献祭餐，其举行总是为了确认共同的宗教信仰。俄耳甫斯教宣扬尊重动物生命并禁食动物肉，这并非偶然。灵魂转世的信仰，最初源自毕达哥拉斯学派，使得这一禁令成为必要。对于俄耳甫斯教徒而言，从罪孽与污染中净化是一种精神上的必需，尤其是因为他们相信，对今世所犯罪行的惩罚是不可避免的。如果惩罚未在人的一生中发生，它必然会在来世降临。俄耳甫斯教徒必须戒绝的事物，会以污秽、污染威胁其灵魂的纯洁。净化，即卡塔西斯，不仅使灵魂摆脱不洁，还保护个人免受惩罚，并给予他在极乐世界获得永生的希望。那些到达冥界及其各种惩罚（均借鉴自希腊神话）的人，将永远留在那里。 他们曾是未得救赎者，注定永远失去灵魂转世的机会，从而无缘救赎。 9 
The supreme god of Orphism was Dionysos, and at the center of this religious faith was a cosmogony different from the one we learn from Hesiod’s Theogony. Orphism preached the simple idea that the world was born from an egg. This primordial egg hatched out the first god, Eros, who was later named Protogonos and Phanes and who was said to be both male and female. He then created the world. The Hesiodic succession of Sky, Kronos, and Zeus was retained. Appended to this was the story of the death of Dionysos at the hands of the Titans, who tore him to pieces and devoured him, and Dionysos’ eventual rebirth.10 This significant theme was reenacted by the ecstatic worshippers of Dionysos. Central to Orphism is the idea that the body is evil and the soul is divine. In fact, the body is a tomb which serves as a prison for the spiritual entity we call the soul. The material part of man, the body, is the evil inheritance of the Titans. The spiritual part, the soul, comes from Dionysos, an immortal god and the son of Zeus. It is obvious that the Homeric concept of the living body as the man himself and of the soul as a pale lifeless shadow of him is completely inverted in Orphism.俄耳甫斯教的至高神是狄俄尼索斯，其信仰核心是一种不同于赫西俄德《神谱》所载的宇宙起源论。该教派宣扬一个朴素观念：世界诞生于一枚卵。这枚原初之卵孵出了第一位神祇厄洛斯——他后来被称为普罗托戈诺斯和法涅斯，传说兼具男女两性特质，随后创造了世界。赫西俄德体系中的天神、克洛诺斯与宙斯的承继关系得以保留，并增补了狄俄尼索斯被泰坦神族撕碎吞噬而后重生的传说。 10 这一重要主题由狄俄尼索斯的狂喜信徒们反复演绎。俄耳甫斯教的核心思想是肉体为恶、灵魂属圣。事实上，肉体如同囚禁灵魂这一精神实体的坟墓。人类物质性的肉体承袭自泰坦的邪恶本源，而精神性的灵魂则源自宙斯之子——不朽之神狄俄尼索斯。显然，荷马史诗中将鲜活肉体视作人本身、将灵魂看作苍白无生命影子的观念，在俄耳甫斯教中遭到了彻底颠覆。
The relation of Orpheus to Dionysus is peculiar. Both are connected with Thrace. Dionysos is a god of transitions.11 Orpheus obviously could cross the boundaries of culture into nature and back. He descended into the underworld to recover his beloved Eurydike and came back alive. The meaning of this myth is twofold. Heavenly song can conquer death and so can devotion to the beloved. But Eurydike, “wide justice,” remains in the world below, desired but tantalizingly beyond the reach of the living. The mythic prophet Orpheus dies a strange death; he is torn to pieces by Thracian maenads. This death is analogous to the one Dionysos himself suffered. Clearly the practice of Dionysian orgies, of tearing wild beasts into pieces and devouring their limbs, is a ritual connected with the tragic dismemberment of Orpheus. Maenadic women also in a state of ecstatic frenzy killed Pentheus, king of Thebes. In so many ways, Pentheus in the story that is so powerfully told by Euripides in the Bacchae is the surrogate victim. Pentheus dies so that Dionysus may live on forever.俄耳甫斯与狄俄尼索斯的关系颇为特殊。两者都与色雷斯地区相关联。狄俄尼索斯是掌管过渡的神祇。 11 俄耳甫斯显然能够跨越文化与自然的界限，并自由往返其间。他曾为寻回挚爱的欧律狄刻而深入冥界，最终生还。这一神话具有双重寓意：天籁之音可以战胜死亡，对爱人的忠贞亦能创造奇迹。但"广袤正义"化身的欧律狄刻仍长眠于冥界，虽令人向往却始终是生者无法触及的存在。这位神话先知俄耳甫斯的死亡方式极为诡异——他被色雷斯的狂女们撕成碎片。这种死法与狄俄尼索斯本人曾遭受的磨难如出一辙。显然，狄俄尼索斯式的狂欢仪式中撕裂野兽吞食肢体的行为，正是与俄耳甫斯悲剧性肢解相关联的宗教仪轨。处于迷狂状态的狂女们同样杀害了忒拜国王彭透斯。在欧里庇得斯于《酒神的伴侣》中浓墨重彩讲述的故事里，彭透斯以多种形式扮演着替罪羊的角色。他的死亡换取了狄俄尼索斯的永恒存续。
Bits and pieces of Orphism are evident throughout the collection, but there is very little about Orphic theogony, anthropogony, or eschatology. To be sure Protogonos is equated with Phanes and is addressed as “born of the egg, delighting in his golden wings” (hymn 6.2). Orphic anthropogony is alluded to in the hymn to the Titans (hymn 37.4–6): “From you are descended all toiling mortals, / the brood of the sea and of the land, then the brood of the birds, / of all generations of the world born of you.” Kronos and Time (Greek khronos) are characteristically equated at hymn 13.5 where Kronos is called “begetter of time.” And certainly the phrase “dreadful Necessity governs all things” (hymn 3.11) must have been pregnant with meaning for the initiate, since Necessity mated with Time to give birth to Ether, Khaos, and Erebos. There is no hint anywhere of animal sacrifices and of meat eating, even if Dionysos himself is addressed as “ōmadios” (“taker of raw flesh”). This we may interpret as a concession to the non-Orphic side of the god and as part of the comprehensiveness of poems that are essentially conjuring formulae. Interestingly enough, it seems to be the persistent Orphic aversion to the crime of ōmophagia (eating of raw flesh and thus also the dismemberment of Dionysos) that accounts for its suppression in the hymn to the Titans (hymn 37). Also Orphic, but not uniquely Orphic, is the sentiment expressed in the varieties of the concluding formula that the addressee grant a good end to a life, since a good life on earth attended by the proper rites of initiation and purification constitutes some sort of guarantee of rewards, or at least of escape from punishment in the afterlife. The idea held by the Orphics that the body was a prison for the soul is expressed in the very last hymn (hymn 87.3–4).12 Referring as it does to a very central and basic belief, it serves as an unmistakably Orphic capstone of an edifice to which other religions and philosophical systems made generous contributions.整部诗集中随处可见俄耳甫斯教的零散痕迹，但关于俄耳甫斯神谱、人类起源论或末世论的内容却极少。诚然，原初之神普罗托戈诺斯等同于法涅斯，并被赞颂为"诞生于卵中，以金色双翼为乐"（第六首颂诗第 2 节）。泰坦颂诗（第三十七首颂诗第 4-6 节）中隐约提及俄耳甫斯人类起源论："所有劳碌的凡人皆由你而生，/海洋与陆地的子嗣，继而飞鸟的后代，/世间万代皆由你孕育而生。"克洛诺斯与时间（希腊语 khronos）在第十三首颂诗第 5 节被典型地等同起来，克洛诺斯被称为"时间的创造者"。而"可怖的必然性统御万物"（第三首颂诗第 11 节）这一表述对入教者必然蕴含深意，因为必然性与时间结合诞生了以太、卡俄斯与厄瑞玻斯。全诗未见任何动物献祭与食肉行为的暗示，即便狄俄尼索斯本人被称为"ōmadios"（"生肉吞噬者"）。我们可将此理解为对这位神灵非俄耳甫斯教属性的妥协，也是这些本质上作为咒语程式的诗歌所具有的包容性体现。 有趣的是，似乎正是俄耳甫斯教对食生肉罪（ōmophagia，即生食血肉，因而也涉及狄俄尼索斯被肢解）的持续厌恶，解释了为何在《提坦颂》（第 37 首颂歌）中这一内容被压制。同样具有俄耳甫斯教特色（但并非其独有）的，是各种结语形式中所表达的情感：祈求受颂者赐予生命以善终。因为尘世的美好生活伴随着适当的入教和净化仪式，构成了某种对死后奖赏的保证，或至少能避免在来世受罚。俄耳甫斯教徒认为身体是灵魂的囚笼，这一观念在最后一首颂歌（第 87 首第 3-4 节）中得以表达。 12 由于它涉及一个非常核心和基本的信仰，它作为一个明确无误的俄耳甫斯教冠石，矗立在其他宗教和哲学体系慷慨贡献的建筑之上。

The question of Orphic rituals is a tantalizing one. Poems such as the Rhapsodies, Argonautika, and Lithika were written in late antiquity. Falsely attributed to Orpheus, they are a fantasy literature whose connection with Orphism ranges from non-existent to tenuous. For Pindar, glorious Orpheus is the father of songs (Pythian Odes 4.176–177). Immortality is conferred by lofty song. No Orphic ritual can emerge from the musings of this most aristocratic Greek poet. The fascination with the Bacchic gold tablets is justifiably enormous. Yet these fabulous fragments do not amount to a text that can help us reconstruct even one Orphic ritual. Immortality of the soul is the key Orphic belief in them. This central Orphic belief, I think, is the dominant theme of the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, composed sometime in the seventh century BC, whose origins specialists in Greek religion trace to an agricultural cult, specifically a fertility ritual. Caution must be exercised here. Syncretism and fusion must not be forgotten. Demeter dips Demophoön into fire to grant him immortality. Demeter’s abducted daughter, Persephone, and her journey to Hades and back into the upper world and into life is a great allegory for death and resurrection and hence a great allegory for immortality. There is frequent mention of ritual in connection with Orphism. Ancient references to Orphism and the Orphics are not very helpful in this regard. The beautiful Orphic cosmogony in the Birds of Aristophanes (685–704) teaches us ideas about the origin of the world. There is nothing in it as to what one should or should not do. There are many references to Orpheus and his followers in Plato, especially in the Republic. They are mostly philosophical speculations about aspects of human eschatology. Orphism inspired Pythagoras to create a rich type of theology that was founded on practice. Various details of the way his followers lived have more to do with a holistic way of life and less with the performance of certain rituals.关于俄耳甫斯仪式的探讨引人入胜。诸如《狂想曲》、《阿尔戈英雄纪》与《石志》等诗篇创作于古代晚期，虽被伪托为俄耳甫斯所作，实属幻想文学，其与俄耳甫斯教派的关联从无迹可寻到若有若无。在品达眼中，荣耀的俄耳甫斯乃是诗歌之父（《皮托竞技胜利颂》4.176-177）。不朽性借崇高诗歌得以赋予。这位最具贵族气质的希腊诗人的沉思冥想中，无法诞生任何俄耳甫斯仪式。人们对酒神金箔的痴迷确有充分理由。然而这些瑰丽碎片远不足以构成能帮助我们重构哪怕一种俄耳甫斯仪式的文本。灵魂不朽正是其中核心的俄耳甫斯信仰。我认为，这一核心信仰正是《荷马颂歌·致得墨忒耳》的主导主题——该颂歌约创作于公元前七世纪，研究希腊宗教的学者将其起源追溯至农业崇拜，具体而言是一种丰产仪式。在此必须保持审慎。融合与交汇的现象不容忽视。得墨忒耳将得摩丰浸入火焰以赐予他不朽之身。 得墨忒耳被掳走的女儿珀耳塞福涅，她前往冥界又重返上界、重获生命的旅程，是死亡与复活的伟大寓言，因而也是不朽的伟大寓言。俄耳甫斯教常与仪式相关联。古代关于俄耳甫斯教及其信徒的记载在这方面并无太大助益。阿里斯托芬《鸟》中优美的俄耳甫斯宇宙起源论（第 685-704 行）向我们传授了关于世界起源的观念。其中并未涉及人应当或不应当做什么。柏拉图著作中多次提及俄耳甫斯及其追随者，尤其在《理想国》中。这些大多是关于人类末世论方面的哲学思辨。俄耳甫斯教启发了毕达哥拉斯，使其创立了一种建立在实践基础上的丰富神学体系。其追随者生活方式的诸多细节，更多关乎整体性的生活方式，而非特定仪式的执行。
The cult of Dionysos was the most widespread in the Hellenized world. Religious associations that honored both Orpheus and Dionysos seem to have existed everywhere, and some rituals were called both Orphic and Dionysian. It seems quite clear from the collection itself that the Hymns were used by such a religious association (thiasos) of people who called themselves mustai, mustipoloi, or orgiophantai (mystic initiates) and who through prayer (eukhē), libation (loibē), sacrifice (thusia), and, presumably, secret ceremonies (orgia, teletai) invoked a series of divinities and asked for their presence or for the gift of some blessing, such as wealth, peace, health, and not infrequently for a blameless end to a good life. These associations had a definite hierarchy. One of the most prominent officiates was the boukolos, the oxherd. This title occurs only twice in the Orphic Hymns: at hymn 1.10 and hymn 31.7. It is reasonable to assume that the underlying idea was that of the mediator who would help the initiates into a Dionysian transformation. And it is equally reasonable to assume that a newly founded thiasos commissioned one or more able poets to provide them with religious poetry that should be as authentic and comprehensive as possible.狄俄尼索斯崇拜在希腊化世界中最为盛行。尊崇俄耳甫斯与狄俄尼索斯的宗教团体似乎遍布各地，某些仪式同时被称为俄耳甫斯式与狄俄尼索斯式。从《俄耳甫斯颂歌》集本身可以明确看出，这些颂歌被一个自称为"慕斯塔伊"、"慕斯提波洛伊"或"奥吉奥梵泰"（意为秘仪入会者）的宗教团体（提亚索斯）所使用。他们通过祈祷、奠酒、献祭以及（据推测）秘密仪式，召唤一系列神明，祈求神祇降临或赐予福祉——诸如财富、和平、健康，且时常祈求善终无瑕。这些团体具有明确的等级制度。其中最重要的司仪之一是"布科洛斯"，即牧牛人。这个头衔在《俄耳甫斯颂歌》中仅出现两次：第一颂第 10 行与第三十一颂第 7 行。有理由认为，其深层理念在于牧牛人作为中介者，将协助入会者完成狄俄尼索斯式的转化。 同样合理的假设是，一个新成立的宗教团体委托一位或多位有才华的诗人，为他们创作尽可能真实且全面的宗教诗歌。
Most of the Hymns are addressed to divinities and concepts of the Hellenistic pantheon and its train of lesser divine or semi-divine figures. Such personified abstractions as Dike, Justice, and Nomos are so old and so common to various schools of Greek philosophical and religious thought as not to be especially Orphic. The only hymn to a god of Near Eastern origin is the one to Adonis. Three hymns are dedicated to Anatolian goddesses (Mise, Hipta, Melinoe), and the Anatolian moon god Men is mentioned in the opening address to Mousaios. The Orphic sympathies of the collection are nowhere more evident than in the number and fervor of individual pieces addressed to Dionysos. There are seven such hymns (possibly nine, if Mise and Korybas are viewed as alternate manifestations of Dionysos), while Zeus has only three that are specifically addressed to him. Dionysos is also frequently invoked or alluded to in many other hymns, and his characteristic epithets seem to have been so infectious and to have assumed such universal significance as to seriously have encroached on the territory of other deities (see further hymn 30). This is as it should be, since Dionysos is the chief Orphic god.大多数颂歌都献给希腊化万神殿的神祇与概念，以及一系列次要的神性或半神性形象。诸如狄刻（正义）与诺摩斯（律法）这类拟人化的抽象概念在希腊哲学与宗教思想的各个流派中历史悠久且普遍存在，并非特别具有俄耳甫斯教派的特色。唯一一首献给近东起源神祇的颂歌是献给阿多尼斯的。有三首颂歌专门献给安纳托利亚女神（密塞、希普塔、墨利诺厄），而在对穆赛俄斯的开篇致辞中提到了安纳托利亚的月神门。这部诗集中俄耳甫斯教派的倾向性，在献给狄俄尼索斯的篇章数量与热情程度上体现得最为明显。此类颂歌共有七首（若将密塞与科律巴斯视为狄俄尼索斯的另类显现，则可能达九首），而宙斯仅有三首专门献给他的颂歌。狄俄尼索斯还在其他许多颂歌中被频繁召唤或提及，其特有的称号似乎具有极强的感染力，并获得了如此普遍的意义，以至于严重侵入了其他神祇的领域（详见第 30 首颂歌）。这实属应当，因为狄俄尼索斯是俄耳甫斯教派的主神。
The Hymns were devotional. Perfumes are frequently mentioned at the beginning of an individual hymn. Sometimes incense is mentioned specifically. Storax was imported from Phoenicia, while incense and myrrh came from the Arabian Peninsula. There seems to have been a certain protocol, and a preference for this or that kind of aromatic substance. Incense for Sun, frankincense for Nike, Apollon, Artemis, Dionysos Liknites, and several other divinities. Myrrh was offered to Protogonos, Poseidon, Nereus, and Leto; storax to Prothyraia, Kronos, Zeus, Proteus, Dionysos, Demeter, Chthonic Hermes, etc. Crocus was offered to Ether, opium to Sleep, and simply perfumes for Moon, Physis, Rhea, Athene, etc. As has been observed it is not easy to see the connection between specific aromatic substances and ritualistic practices. The variety might be attributed to the preference of persons who contributed the specific perfume or other material. Perhaps also the season of the year played a role. The distribution of perfumes and aromatic substances as they appear in our Hymns is such as to make it impossible for us to offer a rational explanation of any systematic organization.这些颂歌具有虔诚的宗教性质。在每首颂歌的开篇，常提及香料的使用。有时会特别提到熏香。苏合香从腓尼基进口，而乳香和没药则来自阿拉伯半岛。似乎存在某种特定的仪式规范，以及对不同芳香物质的偏好。太阳神享用熏香，胜利女神尼刻、阿波罗、阿尔忒弥斯、狄俄尼索斯·利克尼特斯及其他几位神祇则享用乳香。没药献给原初之神普罗托戈诺斯、波塞冬、涅柔斯和勒托；苏合香献给普罗提拉亚、克洛诺斯、宙斯、普罗透斯、狄俄尼索斯、得墨忒耳、冥界赫尔墨斯等。番红花献给以太，罂粟献给睡眠之神，而月亮女神、自然女神菲西斯、瑞亚、雅典娜等则享用普通的香料。正如观察所见，特定的芳香物质与仪式实践之间的联系并不容易理解。这种多样性可能归因于贡献特定香料或其他材料者的个人偏好。或许季节因素也起到了一定作用。我们颂歌中出现的香料和芳香物质的分布情况，使我们无法对其系统性组织提供合理的解释。
It makes sense to think that the time of chanting these beautiful hymns was evening. For the initiates the day’s labor was done and their worries could be set aside for the replenishment of their souls and for a respite from the mundane realities of the world. The Hymns are redolent with elements of mysticism. Indeed, the most pervasive characteristic of the Hymns, the ubiquitous epithet, might be, in part, an indication of a link between these hymns and the various remains of magic literature from the Hellenistic and Roman periods. Both direct a propitiatory address to a deity, accompanied by as comprehensive a list of its powers and properties as possible. The difference is that where the initiate seeks to persuade and cajole, the sorcerer seeks to bind and compel. There is no indication of accompanying music in the Hymns; however, it would be a mistake to latch onto this omission and think there was no music. First of all, the hymns themselves chanted properly constituted music. Perhaps that was enough for the initiates. Percussion instruments are mentioned, but their appearance might be due to their traditional associations. It is not easy to settle this question. Indic, Iranian, and Muslim cult music should not be excluded from consideration. After all, all these traditions use song as a bridge by which to unite heaven and earth. It should also be recalled that Orpheus was famous as a poet and a singer in addition to being renowned for his role as legendary founder of mystic rites.可以合理地推测，吟唱这些优美赞歌的时间是在夜晚。对于信徒而言，白日的劳作已经结束，他们可以将忧虑暂时搁置，以滋养灵魂，从世俗的现实中获得片刻喘息。这些赞歌充满了神秘主义的元素。事实上，赞歌中最普遍的特征——无处不在的修饰语——可能部分地暗示了这些赞歌与希腊化和罗马时期各种魔法文献遗存之间的联系。两者都向神明发出安抚的致辞，并尽可能全面地列举其力量和属性。区别在于，信徒寻求的是说服和劝诱，而巫师则试图束缚和强迫。赞歌中没有提及伴奏音乐；然而，抓住这一疏漏并认为没有音乐是错误的。首先，赞歌本身若被恰当地吟唱，便构成了音乐。或许这对信徒来说已经足够。虽然提到了打击乐器，但它们的存在可能源于传统的联想。要解决这个问题并不容易。 印度、伊朗和伊斯兰教的祭祀音乐也不应被排除在考量之外。毕竟，所有这些传统都使用歌曲作为连接天地的桥梁。同样应当铭记的是，俄耳甫斯除了作为神秘仪式的传奇创始人而闻名外，还以诗人和歌手的身份著称。
We cannot recover the sounds and we do not know exactly what the mood was when the Hymns were sung. It might not be too much to suggest that people gathered in places that were sacred to them and that they did so as the softer colors of the evening were settling in on them. Candles provided gentle light. Wisps of incense smoke rose into the air. On the whole, the style of the Hymns is homogenous and consistent. At the beginning of each hymn, the invocation, sometimes several divinities are summoned. Usually the name of the divinity or divinities is followed by an imperative, e.g., “Come! Hear!” Variations are to be found in the end of the prayer that asks for blessing, peace, prosperity, and wealth. There appears to be an order to the arrangement of most of the hymns. There are many male/female pairings throughout.13 The opening ones focus on the gods of the early generations and the theme of birth. Physis, Pan, and Herakles form a triad that sums up the creation of the physical world. Kronos and Rhea lead to Zeus. This begins a series of hymns where the traditional four elements of fire, air, water, and earth provide a coherent structure (hymns 15–27). Everything leads to the first hymn to Dionysos (hymn 30), his “birth” in a sense, which is strengthened by the appearance of divinities connected with the Orphic myth of his birth, death, and rebirth (hymns 31–38). A block of four hymns treats Eleusinian themes (hymns 40–43), and then comes the central cluster of hymns treating Dionysian cult (hymns 44–54). Aphrodite seems to preside over another series (hymns 55–68). A number of minor divinities, mostly in pairs and all of cultic importance, continue to another grouping of hymns associated with the elements (hymns 79–84). The three brothers Sleep, Dream, and Death end the collection. For details, see the introductions to the various individual hymns. The Hymns are catalogues of religious epithets; such catalogues are intended to evoke the many powers of various divinities that are significant to a particular type of religious ideology and practice. The question is: what sources of ancient literature could have inspired and instructed the writers of the Hymns? We have already indicated magical incantations. Hesiod’s catalogues of the daughters of Nereus and of the daughters of Okeanos are religious documents (Theogony 240–264 and 346–363). Homer’s catalogue of the Nereids (Iliad 18.39–49) is a poetic construct, whose origin is religious. Hesiod’s catalogues come from an old religious tradition. A deity must be invoked by words that refer to its attributes. In all likelihood the names of the daughters of Nereus and of the daughters of Okeanos are in fact epithets of the sea, at times older than even Hesiod, epithets that point to a Mother of the Waters. The sea has countless potencies, countless faces. The sea is both a great blessing and a treacherous element that is fraught with peril. The fact that great numbers of feminine divinities, essentially Daughters of the Sea, so frequently rise out of the sea is indicative of a deeply entrenched and old religious feeling that the sea is feminine and maternal, a huge counterpart to the masculine sky. Zeus is the Indo-European sky god. When people pray to him they also pray to the sky. In a tradition that predates the arrival of the Greeks in Greece, the sea and its in-dwelling divinities must have received more attention. The new religion that emerged introduced a male god whose dominion became preeminent. The lists of the daughters of Nereus and of Okeanos are prayer lists that come from an older religious order. Every one of these names has a meaning. Even a casual look at these texts shows that they are religious texts that have one main thing in common: they are strings of nouns or epithets addressed to a divinity. A first approach to them leaves the reader puzzled as to their aesthetic, that is to say their poetic value, as well as to their effectiveness. However, here is a suggestion to readers of the Hesiodic catalogues as well as of the Orphic Hymns. They are asked to raise their voices as they read to a pleasant and imposing pitch as well as a clear and rhythmically punctuated vocalization of the lines. The tone of voice should strive to approximate dignified chant. Examples are to be found in many cultures. If all this is done, the religious character of the catalogues comes alive. They are no longer boring, and their invocational nature becomes entirely clear.即使对这些文本稍加审视，也能看出它们是宗教文本，有一个主要的共同点：它们是一连串指向神祇的名词或称号。初次接触这些文本时，读者会对其美学价值，即其诗歌价值，以及其有效性感到困惑。然而，这里对阅读赫西俄德目录和俄耳甫斯颂歌的读者提出一个建议。他们被要求在阅读时提高声音，达到一种悦耳而庄重的音调，同时清晰而有节奏地诵读这些诗句。声音的语调应努力接近庄严的吟唱。许多文化中都能找到这样的例子。如果做到这一切，这些目录的宗教特性就会变得生动起来。它们不再枯燥乏味，其召唤的本质也变得完全清晰。
Every Greek is aware that the Virgin Mary is addressed by various names that have become sacred names. When I [A.N.A.] was working on the Hesiodic and Homeric lists, I decided to find out just how many names were used to address the Virgin Mary in the Hellenic world. I walked into a fine bookshop in Athens, and to my astonishment I discovered four beautiful volumes devoted to an explanation of the nearly five hundred names by which the Virgin Mary is addressed. This rich tradition may indeed ultimately go back even to pre-Hellenic times. The idea suggested here is that the veneration of the Virgin Mary has inherited aspects of the veneration of the sea and its divinities in prehistoric time. Here is just a sample of names which refer to the Virgin Mary: She of the Shoreline, She of the Sea Calm, the Far Heard One, She of the Seas, She of the Lakes, She of the Harbors, She of the Caves, She of the Rivers, She of Good Sailing. It should not be too difficult for anyone to hear in this sample echoes from Hesiod’s catalogues of the Nereids. The astonishing number of epithets to the Virgin Mary in the Hellenic lands should not be regarded as some sort of random religious occurrence. Whether the attributes of a divinity are described by epithets, nouns, or periphrastic expressions makes no substantial difference. Relevant here from the Judaic tradition is Exodus 34:6–7 in which God Himself speaks of his own attributes. Muslims believe in one God whose divine qualities are known to them by ninety-nine (some say more) different names.14 Numbers 12–19 in Siddiqi read as follows: The Rightful / The Fashioner of Forms / The Ever-Forgiving / The All-Compelling Subduer / The Bestower / The Ever-Providing / The Opener / The Victory-Giver / The All-Knowing. However, these sacred names appear throughout the Koran and in this respect they do not resemble the Hesiodic catalogues or the Orphic Hymns. It is not so much the semantic content as the tone and cumulative effect of this religious utterance that opens possibilities of comparison with the Hymns. The emotionally powerful, indeed ecstatic and repetitive, invocation of Allah by the Whirling Dervishes of the Mevlevi Order dominates the performance of their rituals. The ninety-nine names of Allah are recited in their daily prayers and meditations. Such practices cannot be so very different from the concept and practice of unceasing prayer, such as the Jesus Prayer, so central to the monastic life of Mount Athos. His spiritual teachings took root in Konya, Turkey, not too far from ancient Pergamum, the city that may have produced the Orphic Hymns. The Orphic Hymns name specific pagan divinities, yet they appeal to universal spiritual powers. Some of them, like the hymns to Dream, Death, and Sleep, are in essence prayers that could be offered to God regardless of specific faith. All this makes excellent sense. The years between 300 and 500 AD were years of transition. It is very naïve to think that the Christian faith simply walked into towns, villages, and hamlets to be triumphantly received. It is much likelier that the new faith made accommodations with places and associations that cultivated the spiritual values. The new faith lacked the language of expressing the new spiritual values. The old faith, especially as expressed in documents like the Hymns, possessed a liturgical language ready to be used. Echoes of the compositional mode of the Hymns, especially of the effect of clustering epithets, can occasionally be heard in the great devotional and, at the same time invocational, Hymns of the Orthodox Church, such as the Akathistos Hymnos: “Spotless, pollutionless, incorruptible, untouched, pure Virgin, Despoina, Bride of God.”《俄耳甫斯颂歌》虽指名道姓地呼唤异教诸神，实则诉诸普世性的灵性力量。其中部分篇章——如献给梦境、死亡与睡眠的颂歌——本质上是超越具体信仰、可向任何神明呈献的祷词。这一切都合乎情理。公元 300 至 500 年间正值信仰过渡期。若认为基督教信仰仅是长驱直入城镇乡村便赢得万众归心，未免过于天真。更可能的情形是：新兴信仰与那些培育灵性价值的场所及团体达成了融合。新兴信仰缺乏表达崭新灵性价值的语言体系，而古老信仰——尤其体现于《颂歌》这类文献中——却拥有现成的礼仪语言。在正教会那些兼具虔敬与召唤特质的伟大颂歌中，偶尔仍可听见《俄耳甫斯颂歌》创作模式的回响，特别是密集使用称号的手法，例如《阿卡菲斯托斯颂》中的诗句：“无瑕无疵、不染污浊、永不朽坏、未经触碰的纯洁童女，主宰者，神的新娘。”
The Orphic Hymns, as well as similar hymns, have neither plot nor action. They are not at all like the major Homeric hymns in that they do not appeal to any emotion. None of our hymns shows even a trace of humor, rhetorical conceit, or for that matter a desire to delight or shock the initiates. Clearly, elevation of mood and the powerful affirmation of a meaningful and bonding presence are elements that run through the recitation of mighty words and sacred sounds flowing into the eager ears and souls of the faithful. Even the puns serve this purpose. Names chanted or better yet sung or even simply recited in a particular sacred tone have power. Each epithet reverberates into the mind of the celebrant and spins out its own plot and its own action. As one epithet follows another, chains of meaning and sound acquire a power that may exceed that of a highly structured narrative. One name is one thing. Two names are more than two things. The Orphic Hymns are beautiful poetry of another kind, a transcendental kind, which must be understood in the context of its own conventions.俄耳甫斯颂歌，以及类似的颂歌，既无情节也无行动。它们与荷马式的主要颂歌截然不同，因为它们不诉诸任何情感。我们的颂歌中甚至没有一丝幽默、修辞自负，或者取悦或震惊入门者的意图。显然，情绪的高涨以及对有意义且具有联结性的存在的强烈肯定，是贯穿于强大词语和神圣声音朗诵中的元素，这些声音流入信徒们渴望的耳朵和灵魂。即使是双关语也服务于这一目的。以特定神圣音调吟唱、或更好是歌唱、甚至仅仅是朗诵的名字具有力量。每个称号在庆祝者的心中回响，并展开自己的情节和行动。当一个称号接一个称号时，意义和声音的链条获得了一种可能超越高度结构化叙事的力量。一个名字是一件事。两个名字不仅仅是两件事。俄耳甫斯颂歌是另一种美丽的诗歌，一种超越性的诗歌，必须在它自己的惯例背景下理解。

Orpheus to Mousaios俄耳甫斯致穆赛俄斯
The opening poem of the collection portrays the fiction of Orpheus instructing Mousaios in a rite. A loose parallel may be adduced in the case of Hesiod, who tells us of his transformation from shepherd to poet in the beginning of the Theogony (1–114); note in particular how the Muses there are initially described singing a hymn to a list of divinities (11–21), similar to what we find in this poem. Inclusivity is a characteristic of Greek polytheism, and it can be dangerous to omit the wrong divinity. This is a recurring theme in myth (e.g., the Kalydonian Boar because Artemis was neglected, the infidelity of Helen and her sister Klytemnestra because Aphrodite was neglected, the apple in the Judgment of Paris because Strife was snubbed).这部诗集的开篇诗描绘了俄耳甫斯教导穆赛俄斯进行仪式的虚构场景。赫西俄德的情况可作为一个松散的类比，他在《神谱》开头（1-114 行）讲述了自己从牧羊人转变为诗人的经历；尤其值得注意的是，缪斯女神在那里最初被描述为向一系列神灵唱诵赞歌（11-21 行），这与本诗中的内容相似。包容性是希腊多神教的特征，而遗漏错误的神灵可能带来危险。这是神话中反复出现的主题（例如，因忽视阿尔忒弥斯而引发的卡吕冬野猪事件，因忽视阿佛洛狄忒而导致海伦及其姐妹克吕泰涅斯特拉的不忠，因怠慢纷争女神而在帕里斯的评判中出现的金苹果）。
For Orpheus, see the introduction to the translation. Mousaios was also a semi-legendary figure of questionable antiquity who was thought to be both a poet (his name means “of the Muse”) and a founder of religious rites. He was considered to be the father of Eumolpos, the eponymous ancestor of the Eumolpids, one of the two hereditary families entrusted to administrating the Eleusinian Mysteries (see OH 40i). Mousaios seems to have been originally independent of Orpheus but later was made his son and/or disciple. The address “friend” here suggests at least the latter. For more on Mousaios, see West 1983, pp. 39–44.关于俄耳甫斯，请参阅译本的引言。穆赛俄斯同样是一位年代存疑的半传奇人物，被认为既是诗人（其名意为“缪斯之子”），也是宗教仪式的创立者。他被视为欧摩尔波斯的父亲，而欧摩尔波斯是负责管理厄琉息斯秘仪的两个世袭家族之一——欧摩尔波斯家族的同名祖先（参见《俄耳甫斯祷歌》第 40 首注释）。穆赛俄斯最初似乎独立于俄耳甫斯，但后来被设定为他的儿子和/或门徒。此处称呼“朋友”至少暗示了后一种关系。关于穆赛俄斯的更多信息，请参阅韦斯特 1983 年著作第 39 至 44 页。
There is a question whether this poem belongs with our collection or was added at some later date after the Hymns had been made part of a greater compilation of ancient hymns. It will become immediately apparent that the order of divinities in this poem does not, for the most part, match the order of the hymns to individual deities. Furthermore, some personalities, such as Hebe, are mentioned only in this poem, while others who have a hymn devoted to them in the collection, such as Hestia, do not appear here. West argues that this opening address to Mousaios was not part of the original collection but instead might have been the Thuēpolikon (Sacrifice or Mystic Rites) mentioned among the works of Orpheus in the Souda, a tenth-century AD Byzantine lexicon/encyclopedia (West 1968, pp. 288–289). However, the arguments against originality are certainly not insurmountable. For example, given how interconnected various hymns are (through language and motif), the opening may have been felt comprehensive enough despite the discrepancy between the divinities invoked in it and those that receive hymns in the rest of the collection. Another possibility is that the poem was an independent entity that our composer somewhat inartfully grafted onto his efforts. The opening and closing lines could easily have been altered from, and/or added to, the original. Indeed, the original might even have been the inspiration for creating a series of hymns dedicated to individual entities, and the collection could then be viewed as an (imperfect) expansion of it, adapted to the exigencies of the particular ritual in which it was performed.关于这首诗是否属于我们的合集，还是在《颂歌》被纳入更宏大的古代颂歌汇编后于某个较晚时期添加的，存在疑问。可以立即看出，这首诗中神祇的顺序在很大程度上与针对个别神祇的颂歌顺序不符。此外，一些人物，如赫柏，仅在此诗中被提及，而其他在合集中拥有专属颂歌的神祇，如赫斯提亚，却未在此出现。韦斯特认为，这首开篇致穆萨俄斯的诗并非原始合集的一部分，反而可能是苏达（一部公元十世纪的拜占庭词典/百科全书）中提到的俄耳甫斯作品中的《献祭或神秘仪式》（韦斯特，1968 年，第 288-289 页）。然而，反对其原创性的论点并非不可逾越。例如，考虑到各颂歌之间（通过语言和主题）的相互关联，尽管开篇诗所召唤的神祇与合集中其他颂歌所献祭的神祇存在差异，但开篇部分可能已被认为足够全面。 另一种可能性是，这首诗本身是一个独立的实体，我们的作曲家将其略显生硬地嫁接于自己的创作之中。开头和结尾的诗句很可能是在原作基础上进行了修改和/或增补。事实上，原作甚至可能激发了创作一系列献给独立实体的赞美诗的灵感，而这部诗集则可被视为对原作的一种（不完美的）扩展，以适应特定仪式表演的实际需求。
It should also be pointed out that the fiction presented here of the master Orpheus passing on wisdom to his disciple Mousaios would have had great significance for the initiates. Beyond the fancy that attributing the rite to the august figure Orpheus lends the whole affair an aura of prestige and legitimacy, in the performance of this poem it is not only Mousaios who is the beneficiary of Orpheus’ special knowledge but also the initiates themselves. The poem could represent the foundational act of the ritual and have been felt to provide the raison d’être for the cult’s existence. There might be an element of play-acting here, of taking on another role, something that is prevalent in Dionysian worship (see OH 30i). One wonders if it was not the group but a figure of authority (the “oxherd”?) who opened the ceremony by chanting these verses in the guise of Orpheus. We find the theme of foundation of rites appearing intermittently throughout the collection; see OH 76.7n. It is perhaps significant that many such instances involve groups, which might also be serving to break down the divide of mythic past and present reality.还需指出的是，此处虚构的俄耳甫斯大师向其弟子穆赛俄斯传授智慧的设定，对入会者具有重大意义。除了将仪式归功于尊贵的俄耳甫斯能为整个活动增添威望与合法性的想象外，在这首诗的演绎中，不仅是穆赛俄斯，入会者自身也成为俄耳甫斯特殊知识的受益者。这首诗可能代表了仪式的奠基行为，并被视为此教派存在的根本缘由。其中或许存在某种角色扮演的成分——这在狄俄尼索斯崇拜中颇为盛行（参见《俄耳甫斯祷歌》30i 注）。我们不禁猜想，是否并非群体，而是某位权威人物（"牧牛人"？）以俄耳甫斯的身份吟诵这些诗句来开启仪式。我们发现仪式奠基的主题在整部诗集中断续出现；参见《俄耳甫斯祷歌》76.7 注。值得注意的是，许多此类实例涉及群体活动，这可能也有助于消解神话过去与现实当下的隔阂。

41 Beginning and End: These appear to be nothing more than abstractions of philosophical terms. A papyrus fragment containing a commentary on a poem of Alkman that is no longer extant reveals a cosmogony that started from undifferentiated matter that was given form through Poros (Way) and Tekmor (End, Limit), which the commentator interprets as signifying the beginning and end of things (PMGF 5 fr. 2 col. iii; translation and discussion in Kirk, Raven, and Schofield 1983, pp. 47–49). In all three extant versions of an Orphic hymn to Zeus, the god is described as being the first and last (see OH 15.3–5n), and in OH 15.7 he is called “the beginning and end of all” (and see note; however, the Greek word for “end” there is different than the one found here). It is perhaps no surprise, then, that Zeus begins the list of deities in this poem. He may even be understood as Beginning and End here, which would neatly close the long list of divinities in this poem by ring composition. Note, too, that the word “rite” (Greek “thuēpoliē”) appears in the first and last line.41 起始与终结：这些似乎只是哲学术语的抽象概念。一份包含对阿尔克曼已失传诗歌评注的纸莎草残片揭示了一种宇宙起源论，该理论始于未分化的物质，通过波罗斯（途径）和特克莫尔（终结、界限）获得形态，评注者将其解释为事物起始与终结的象征（PMGF 5 fr. 2 col. iii；翻译与讨论见柯克、雷文与斯科菲尔德 1983 年著作，第 47-49 页）。在现存三版俄耳甫斯派献给宙斯的颂诗中，这位神祇均被描述为最初与最终者（参见 OH 15.3–5 注释），在 OH 15.7 中他更被称为“万物的起始与终结”（参见注释；但该处希腊语“终结”用词与此处不同）。因此宙斯在这首诗的神祇名录中居于首位或许并不令人意外。他甚至可被理解为这里的“起始与终结”，通过环形结构精巧地收束了诗中漫长的神祇序列。另需注意，“仪式”（希腊语“thuēpoliē”）一词同时出现在诗篇的首行与末行。
1. To Hekate1. 致赫卡忒
Hekate is a murky goddess on the fringes of Greek religion, and it is very possible that she was originally a native goddess of the Karians, a people in Asia Minor. Her earliest mention is in Hesiod’s Theogony, a relatively long digression of such effusive praise that it is often referred to as a “hymn to Hekate” (411–452). Hesiod asserts that Zeus did not strip her of the honors she held before the defeat of the Titans, among whom she numbers. The poet then goes on to list the wide-ranging powers of the goddess and whom she can help or hinder as she pleases: kings, men speaking in assemblies, soldiers in battle, athletes at competitions, horsemen, sailors (along with Poseidon), and fishermen. Along with Hermes, she can bring fertility or sterility to flocks, and her role in nurturing youths closes out this astounding list of domains. Hesiod also stresses the fact that she is an only child. This picture of Hekate is unique in extant literature. Later on she was frequently identified with Artemis and Moon; see OH 9i and OH 36i. Hesiod perhaps is already moving in this direction, as he calls her a “nurturer of youths,” an epithet usually applied to Artemis (cf. OH 36.8). Moreover, in Hesiod’s genealogies, Hekate is first cousin to Artemis and Apollon, since their mothers, Asteria and Leto respectively, are sisters (Theogony 404–409). The connection with Moon is already suggested in another early poem, the Homeric Hymn to Demeter. After Persephone had been snatched by Hades, Hekate approaches Demeter and informs her that she heard the screams of the abducted girl but did not see the perpetrator (2.51–61). This information is supplied by Sun (2.62–90). Hekate is described as “carrying a light in her hands” (2.52), and, as the female counterpart to Sun in their role as witnesses, seems to be imagined as the moon goddess in these lines; see OH 2i and OH 9.3+n. Note, too, that the name of her mother in Hesiod’s genealogy, Asteria, means “starry.”赫卡忒是希腊宗教边缘的一位神秘女神，很可能最初是小亚细亚卡里亚人的本土女神。她最早出现在赫西俄德的《神谱》中，其中有一段相对较长的离题赞美，常被称为“赫卡忒颂歌”（411-452 行）。赫西俄德声称，宙斯并未剥夺她在泰坦战败前所拥有的荣誉，而她本人也属于泰坦之列。诗人接着列举了这位女神广泛的权力，以及她可以随心所欲地帮助或阻碍的对象：国王、在集会中发言的人、战场上的士兵、竞技场上的运动员、骑手、水手（与波塞冬一起）以及渔民。与赫尔墨斯一起，她能为畜群带来丰产或不育，而她养育青年的角色则结束了这一系列令人惊叹的领域。赫西俄德还强调了她是个独生女的事实。赫卡忒的这一形象在现存文献中是独一无二的。后来，她常与阿尔忒弥斯和月亮女神等同；参见《俄耳甫斯颂歌》9i 和 36i。赫西俄德或许已经朝这个方向迈进，因为他称她为“青年的养育者”，这一称号通常用于阿尔忒弥斯（参见《俄耳甫斯颂歌》36.8）。 此外，在赫西俄德的谱系中，赫卡忒是阿尔忒弥斯和阿波罗的表亲，因为她们的母亲——分别是阿斯忒里亚和勒托——是姐妹（《神谱》404-409）。与月亮的关联在另一首早期诗歌《荷马颂歌·致得墨忒耳》中已有暗示。在珀耳塞福涅被哈迪斯掳走后，赫卡忒接近得墨忒耳并告知她，自己听到了被掳女孩的尖叫但未见到行凶者（2.51-61）。这一信息由太阳神提供（2.62-90）。赫卡忒被描述为“手持光芒”（2.52），并且，作为太阳神在见证者角色上的女性对应者，在这些诗句中似乎被想象为月亮女神；参见《俄耳甫斯颂歌》2i 和 9.3+n。还需注意，赫西俄德谱系中她母亲的名字阿斯忒里亚意为“星辰的”。”
Thus in early Greek literature Hekate had definite celestial connections. But her association in Hesiod with fertility hints at chthonic relations, as does her connection in the story of the abduction of Persephone. When mother and daughter are reunited in the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, Hekate joins in their celebration and becomes Persephone’s “attendant and follower” (2.438–440). She is therefore connected with the world of the dead, and it is this attribute that comes to dominate her aspect in later times. In the magical papyri, she is also explicitly equated with Persephone, along with other entities such as the Fates (PGM 4.2714–2783 and 2785–2870). No longer is she a (potentially) beneficial deity that might deign to grant a person blessings; instead she has become a sinister and dangerous, sometimes demonic, creature of the night (compare lines 5–6 of this hymn). Madness (cf. OH 71i), suffering, and death are her gifts, and she is often described in bestial terms. 2. To Prothyraia2. 致普罗提拉
“Prothyraia” literally means “at the door” or “at the door-way.” There is no goddess proper with this name. The word is a cult title shared by Eileithyia, Artemis, and even Hekate. Our hymn identifies her primarily as Eileithyia, the goddess of childbirth, who assists women in labor and who is invoked for a smooth delivery. Giving birth was fraught with danger in antiquity both for the woman and the child; compare Medeia’s famous assertion that she would rather stand in battle three times than to give birth once (Euripides Medeia 250–251). Artemis was also connected with childbirth (see OH 36.8), and this hymn explicitly equates all three goddesses at line 13. The chorus in Aeschylus’ Suppliant Women prays to Artemis-Hekate as the goddess who protects women in childbirth (674–677). Moon, who is often identified with Artemis and Hekate, is called Eileithyia by Nonnus (Dionysiaca 38.150)."Prothyraia"字面意思是"在门口"或"在门道处"。并没有一个正式以此为名的女神。这个词是伊莱西亚、阿尔忒弥斯乃至赫卡忒共享的祭祀称号。我们的颂诗主要将她认定为分娩女神伊莱西亚，这位女神协助产妇分娩，人们祈求她能带来顺利生产。在古代，分娩对母亲和婴儿都充满危险；可对比美狄亚著名的宣言：她宁愿上战场三次也不愿分娩一次（欧里庇得斯《美狄亚》250-251 行）。阿尔忒弥斯也与分娩相关（参见《俄耳甫斯颂诗》36.8），本颂诗第 13 行明确将三位女神等同。埃斯库罗斯《乞援人》中的歌队向阿尔忒弥斯-赫卡忒祈祷，称其为保护分娩妇女的女神（674-677 行）。诺努斯在《狄奥尼西卡》（38.150）中将常与阿尔忒弥斯和赫卡忒混同的月神称为伊莱西亚。
In myth and literature, Eileithyia is limited to her role in helping childbirth, most famously in the Homeric Hymn to Apollon (3.97–116). Hera, angry at Leto for having been impregnated by Zeus and about to give birth to Apollon, prevents Eileithyia from hearing about Leto, who is suffering greatly on the island of Delos, since she cannot give birth until Eileithyia comes. The other goddesses send Iris with a bribe to coax Eileithyia from Olympos. As soon as the goddess sets foot on the island, Leto goes into labor. In Ovid’s account of the birth of Herakles (Metamorphoses 9.273–323), Eileithyia (spelled Ilithyia and also called by her Roman name, Lucina) sits by an altar outside the door of the house of the pregnant woman. This is a case of sympathetic magic, where the goddess’ position represents the blocking of the infant’s passage out of the womb. Galanthis, a serving girl, is able to trick the goddess into releasing her knees, thus breaking the spell and allowing Herakles to be born. Ovid’s story is quite intriguing, since the goddess is sitting outside the doorway and employing magic. Hera herself has connections with the timing of giving birth, too. The cult of Eileithyia was established on the island and thence spread to the rest of Greece. Pausanias also notes that the Delians sacrificed to Eileithyia and sang a hymn composed by Olen, a legendary poet and prophet—a figure very similar to Orpheus. Pausanias mentions the hymn of Olen in two other passages that suggest that this goddess might have been associated with an older cosmic power. At 9.27.2, Pausanias tells us that in Olen’s hymn Eileithyia is the mother of Eros. Elsewhere, Pausanias remarks that Olen called her “the good spinner” and surmises that Olen identified her with fate (8.21.3). We find a similar connection elsewhere. The position of the hymn in our collection is pregnant with symbolism. There is an emphasis on “birth” in the opening hymns, which are balanced by the last hymn dedicated to Death (see also OH 87i). This might have significance for the actual rite for which our hymns were composed, which probably began after nightfall (see the introduction to the translation and OH 3i). 3. To Night3. 致黑夜
Night (Greek Nux) is personified in Hesiod. She is born from Khaos along with her brother Erebos, with whom she mates and bears Ether and Day (Theogony 123–125; see also OH 5i). Night produces by means of parthenogenesis a brood of personified abstractions, notably for our collection Death, Sleep, and the race of Dreams (Theogony 211–225; cf. lines 5–7 of this hymn and OH 85i). Hesiod also mentions Night in connection with the geography of the underworld. She owns a house, where her children Sleep and Death also live. Day lives there, too, but is never there at the same time at Night; they only greet each other as one leaves and the other returns from the world above (Theogony 744–761; cf. lines 10–11 and see also OH 78.4–5+n). Night perhaps should be seen as belonging to a pre-Olympian generation of divinities in Homer. In the Iliad, as Hera tries to cajole Sleep into inducing Zeus to slumber, Sleep maintains his readiness to bring his gift to all gods, even Okeanos, the father of the gods (14.246, and see OH 83i), but recalls the catastrophe barely averted the last time he put Zeus to sleep against his will. At that time, he escaped the anger of Zeus by the intervention of Night (implied to be Sleep’s mother?), who is described as having power over immortals and mortals and whom Zeus is hesitant to displease (14.256–261). It is not clear what place Night has in Homer’s cosmology, but the respect and fear Zeus shows and feels toward her suggests that Homer considered her to be an old and powerful figure.在赫西俄德的描述中，夜（希腊语 Nux）被拟人化。她与兄弟厄瑞玻斯一同从卡俄斯中诞生，并与之结合，生下了以太和白昼（《神谱》123-125 行；另见 OH 5i）。夜通过单性生殖产生了一系列拟人化的抽象概念，尤其在我们的文集中，包括死亡、睡眠以及梦的种族（《神谱》211-225 行；对照本颂诗第 5-7 行及 OH 85i）。赫西俄德还提到夜与冥界地理相关。她拥有一座房屋，她的孩子睡眠和死亡也居住于此。白昼同样在此居住，但从不与夜同时出现；他们仅在一方离开、另一方从上方世界归来时相互致意（《神谱》744-761 行；对照本颂诗第 10-11 行及 OH 78.4-5+n）。在荷马史诗中，夜或许应被视为属于奥林匹亚神系之前的一代神祇。在《伊利亚特》中，当赫拉试图哄骗睡眠之神诱使宙斯入睡时，睡眠之神表示自己随时准备将这份礼物带给所有神祇，甚至包括众神之父俄刻阿诺斯（14.246 行，另见 OH 83i），但他回忆起上一次违背宙斯意愿使其沉睡时，那场险些酿成的灾难。 当时，他通过夜的干预（暗示是睡眠之母？）逃脱了宙斯的愤怒，夜被描述为拥有对神祇和凡人的掌控力，宙斯也不愿冒犯她（14.256–261）。荷马宇宙观中夜的确切地位并不明确，但宙斯对她表现出的敬畏与恐惧表明，荷马认为她是一位古老而强大的存在。
This is the role she has in various Orphic theogonies, where she is considered to be among the earliest divinities. In light of the Homeric passage, it is first interesting to note that Night gives Zeus oracular advice, e.g., on how to reconstitute the world (Orphic fragment 241; cf. also 113 and 237). In the Rhapsodies there are up to three individual Nights (see West 1983, p. 70, and Betegh 2003, pp. 141–142). The first one existed before Protogonos (Orphic fragment 112–113). Another Night is the daughter of Protogonos (Orphic fragment 148), who later abdicates his throne to her in the symbolic passing of his scepter (Orphic fragment 168–171; see also OH 6i and OH 10.26+n; cf. Iliad 2.100–108 for similar symbolism). She (or a third Night?) also appears as Protogonos’ lover and gives birth to Sky and Earth (Orphic fragment 149; see also OH 4i). In other theogonies similar to those ascribed to Orpheus, Night is one of the oldest, if not the oldest, beings. Mousaios puts her among Tartaros and Aer (fragment 81), while Epimenides places her alongside Aer as the two primeval beings (fragment 46). Aristotle notes that even “the ancient poets” do not claim that the primeval beings (mentioned are Night, Sky, Khaos, and Okeanos) “are king or rule,” but rather Zeus (Metaphysics 1091b4–6). He does not name names, but it is possible that for Okeanos he had Homer in mind, and for Khaos Hesiod. Night and Sky do not correspond to any known theogony, but, the fact that our collection has a hymn to Night as “mother of gods and men” followed by a hymn to Sky who is called “father of all,” suggests that perhaps there was such an Orphic theogony, now lost to us, circulating in antiquity and well known by Aristotle’s time; see OH 4i and also OH O.24, where Night is called “oldest of all.”这是她在各种俄耳甫斯神谱中所扮演的角色，她被视作最早的神祇之一。鉴于荷马史诗中的段落，首先值得注意的是，黑夜给予宙斯神谕建议，例如如何重建世界（俄耳甫斯残篇 241；另见残篇 113 和 237）。在《狂想曲》中，存在多达三个独立的黑夜（参见 West 1983 年，第 70 页，以及 Betegh 2003 年，第 141-142 页）。第一个黑夜存在于原初之神普罗托戈诺斯之前（俄耳甫斯残篇 112-113）。另一个黑夜是普罗托戈诺斯的女儿（俄耳甫斯残篇 148），后来普罗托戈诺斯通过象征性地传递权杖，将王位让给了她（俄耳甫斯残篇 168-171；另见《俄耳甫斯颂歌》6i 和《俄耳甫斯颂歌》10.26+n；类似象征意义可参见《伊利亚特》2.100-108）。她（或是第三个黑夜？）还作为普罗托戈诺斯的情人出现，并生下了天空和大地（俄耳甫斯残篇 149；另见《俄耳甫斯颂歌》4i）。在其他类似于归功于俄耳甫斯的神谱中，黑夜是最古老的存在之一，甚至可能是最古老的存在。穆赛俄斯将她置于塔尔塔罗斯和空气之间（残篇 81），而埃庇米尼得斯则将她与空气并列，视为两个原始存在（残篇 46）。 亚里士多德指出，即便是“古代诗人”也并未声称那些原始存在（文中提及的包括黑夜、天空、混沌和奥克亚诺斯）“是君王或统治者”，而是宙斯（《形而上学》1091b4–6）。他虽未点名道姓，但奥克亚诺斯一词可能源自荷马，而“混沌”一词则可能源自赫西俄德。 “夜”与“天”虽未见于任何已知的神谱，但本集收录的颂歌中，先将“夜”尊为“众神与人类之母”，继而将“天”称为“万物之父”，这一事实暗示着，或许曾存在过这样一部奥尔菲克神谱——虽现已失传，但在古代曾广为流传，且在亚里士多德时代已广为人知； 参见《奥尔菲克颂歌》4i 及 OH O.24，其中“夜”被称为“万物之最古老者”。”
In terms of cultic worship, there are very few instances. Pausanias mentions an oracle of Night on the acropolis of Megara, along with a temple to Dionysos, a temple to Zeus, and a sanctuary to Aphrodite (1.40.6). Note that Night has oracular powers in the Orphic poems, as mentioned already. In Pergamon, where there was a mystery cult to Demeter, religious officials dedicated a number of altars to various gods and goddesses; one official, a hymnetria (a female singer of hymns), is attested to have dedicated an altar to Night, Rites, and Happenstance (see Nilsson 1961, p. 355). The connection between night and rites probably is indicative of the setting of the ritual. Likewise, the early placement of our hymn as well as the appeal at the end for Night to make an appearance before the initiates suggest that the rites for which the collection was written probably began after sunset and proceeded throughout the night (see also OH 54.5+n, OH 78i, OH 86i, and the introduction to the translation).在祭祀崇拜方面，实例极为罕见。保萨尼阿斯提到，在麦加拉的卫城上有一座夜神的神谕所，旁边还有狄俄尼索斯的神庙、宙斯的神庙以及阿芙洛狄忒的圣所（1.40.6）。值得注意的是，正如前文所述，夜神在俄耳甫斯诗歌中拥有预言能力。在佩加蒙，那里有得墨忒耳的神秘崇拜，宗教官员们为众神和女神们奉献了许多祭坛；其中一位官员，一位赞歌女歌手，被证实曾为夜神、仪式和偶然奉献了一座祭坛（参见尼尔森 1961 年，第 355 页）。夜与仪式之间的联系可能暗示了仪式的背景。同样，本赞歌在文集中的早期位置，以及结尾处呼吁夜神在入会者面前显现，都表明这些仪式很可能在日落后开始，并持续整夜进行（另见 OH 54.5+n、OH 78i、OH 86i 及翻译导言）。

4. To Sky4. 致苍穹
Sky (Greek Ouranos) is one of the chief primeval figures in Greek mythology. As a sky god, he is eventually supplanted by his grandson Zeus. In Hesiod’s Theogony, Sky is son and husband of Earth (126–153), and Kronos is their son who, in fact, conspired with Earth to castrate his father (154–210). The marriage between Sky and Earth fits the common mythological motif of the marriage between Father Sky and Mother Earth (see also OH 15i). Their children are the (cosmic) Kyklopes, the Hundred-Handers, and the Titans. Orphic theogony seems to have integrated, or at least borrowed liberally, from the Hesiodic account that had become almost canonical. In the Rhapsodies, Night and Protogonos produce Sky and Earth, who thereupon marry and produce children, including the Fates, Kyklopes, and Hundred-Handers; the Titans, of whom there are fourteen instead of the Hesiodic twelve (added are Phorkys and Dione; for the latter, see OH O.19+n), are born from Earth without the knowledge of Sky. Night raises this brood, and all of the Titans except Okeanos take part in the castration of Sky. As with Hesiod, the Giants and Aphrodite are born from this act (Orphic fragment 149 and 174–189; for Aphrodite Ourania, see OH O.40n and OH 55i+1n). In another version, Sky and Earth are born from the two halves of the egg out of which Protogonos is hatched; see OH 6.2n. Sky appears on the Bacchic gold tablets as well. In no less than twelve the initiate claims to be born of Earth and “starry Sky” (nos. 1, 2, 8, 10–14, 16, 18, 25, 29) and in three of these to be of the “heavenly race” as well (nos. 2, 8, 29; for interpretation, see Graf/Johnston 2007, pp. 111–116). This probably is intended to link the initiate, as a human being, with the Titans, whose destruction by Zeus engendered the human race (see OH 37i). A further connection between Sky qua “heaven” and human beings might be in the notion that the soul, as the sky, is composed of fire; for this idea, cf. OH 5.3 and see OH 66.9n.天空（希腊语 Ouranos）是希腊神话中主要的原始神祇之一。作为天空之神，他最终被其孙宙斯所取代。在赫西俄德的《神谱》中，天空是大地之子兼配偶（第 126-153 行），而克罗诺斯则是他们的儿子，实际上他与大地合谋阉割了自己的父亲（第 154-210 行）。天空与大地的结合符合"天父地母"这一常见的神话母题（另见《俄耳甫斯颂歌》15i 注释）。他们的子女包括（宇宙）独眼巨人、百臂巨人和泰坦神族。俄耳甫斯神谱似乎融合了——或至少大量借鉴了——几乎成为权威的赫西俄德体系。在《诗篇辑录》中，黑夜与普罗托戈诺斯生下了天空和大地，二者随即结合生子，包括命运女神、独眼巨人与百臂巨人；而泰坦神族（共十四位，不同于赫西俄德体系的十二位，增补了福耳库斯与狄俄涅；关于后者参见《俄耳甫斯颂歌》O.19 注释）则由大地独自孕育，未告知天空。黑夜抚养了这群后代，除俄刻阿诺斯外所有泰坦都参与了阉割天空的行动。 与赫西俄德所述相同，巨人和阿芙洛狄忒皆由此行诞生（俄耳甫斯残篇 149 及 174-189；关于阿芙洛狄忒·乌拉尼亚，参见 OH O.40n 与 OH 55i+1n）。另一版本中，天空与大地从原初之神破壳而出的蛋壳两半中诞生；详见 OH 6.2n。天空形象亦见于酒神金版铭文——不少于十二处记载中，入会者宣称自己诞生于大地与"繁星天空"（编号 1、2、8、10-14、16、18、25、29），其中三处更自称属于"天界族裔"（编号 2、8、29；解读参见 Graf/Johnston 2007, pp. 111-116）。这或许旨在将作为人类的入会者与泰坦神族联结，而宙斯毁灭泰坦之举正孕育了人类种族（参见 OH 37i）。天空作为"天穹"与人类的深层联系，可能源于灵魂如天空般由火元素构成的观念；此观点可对照 OH 5。三、参见 OH 66.9n。
Our hymn does not give much information about Sky’s mythology, although there would be little need since the initiates would know the story, whatever versions they had at their disposal. Instead, Sky is treated here more as the vague personification of a celestial phenomenon. This is not surprising, as Sky in myth is a rather colorless figure whose function seems more to give the later gods an ancient pedigree than to serve as a concrete expression of religious sentiment. Indeed, this might explain why the hymn to Sky appears in this position in the collection and before the one to Ether and Protogonos, both of whom come into existence before Sky. The hymn to Night opens with reference to her role as “mother of gods and men” (OH 3.1), while Sky is called “father of all” right at the start. There are other connections between these two hymns that further reinforce their pairing (see notes passim). It is also suggestive that he is not linked with Earth, as one would expect. Might, then, Sky be invoked as representative of the masculine power of generation, being the oldest such being, paired with Night as the feminine power of generation, also in turn being the oldest of her kind? It would fit the pattern of hymns arranged in male/female pairings, a structural technique found throughout the collection (see OH 14.8–9n). Furthermore, Sky is said to succeed Night in a brief notice found in a commentary on Aristotle’s Metaphysics by Alexander of Aphrodisias, where the order of generation is given as Khaos, Okeanos, Night, Sky, and Zeus, king of the immortal gods (Orphic fragment 370). It is possible that our composer was aware of this or a similar cosmogony and was perhaps influenced by such to give Night a male analogue (see also OH 3i). Sky, then, could be the son and/or junior partner of Night. Be that as it may, the fact remains that this hymn to Sky breaks the sequence Night-Ether-Protogonos that one might have expected based on our extant sources (see further OH 5i).我们的颂歌并未过多涉及天空的神话信息，毕竟入会者早已熟知其故事，无论他们掌握的是哪个版本。相反，这里更多是将天空视为一种天象的模糊拟人化。这并不奇怪，因为神话中的天空形象较为苍白，其作用似乎更多是为后世诸神提供古老谱系，而非作为宗教情感的具体表达。事实上，这或许解释了为何《天空颂》在诗集中出现在这个位置，且排在《以太颂》和《原初神颂》之前——后两者皆先于天空存在。《黑夜颂》开篇即提及她作为“诸神与人类之母”的角色（《俄耳甫斯颂歌》3.1），而《天空颂》起始便称其为“万物之父”。这两首颂歌之间还存在其他联系，进一步强化了它们的对应关系（参见各处注释）。值得注意的是，天空并未如预期般与大地相关联。那么，是否可将天空视为最古老的雄性生殖力象征，与作为最古老雌性生殖力象征的黑夜形成配对？ 这符合男女配对排列的颂诗模式，这种结构手法贯穿整部诗集（参见《俄耳甫斯颂诗》14.8-9 注）。此外，阿弗罗狄西亚的亚历山大在注释亚里士多德《形而上学》时曾简短提及天空继黑夜而生，其中给出的生成顺序为：混沌、俄刻阿诺斯、黑夜、天空，以及不朽众神之王宙斯（俄耳甫斯残篇 370）。本颂诗作者可能知晓这一或类似的宇宙生成论，并受其影响为黑夜设置了男性对应者（另见《俄耳甫斯颂诗》3 引言）。因此，天空可能是黑夜之子及/或从属伴侣。尽管如此，这首献给天空的颂诗确实打破了根据现存文献可能预期的黑夜-以太-原初者序列（详见《俄耳甫斯颂诗》5 引言）。
